title: Fractionalization-Induced Time-Reversal Symmetry Breaking at Continuous Superconducting Transitions in Low-Symmetry Kondo Lattices
abstract: In conventional Landau theory, simultaneous continuous onset of superconductivity and the breaking of additional symmetries generally requires a multidimensional order parameter or fine tuning. We show that symmetry fractionalization provides a different route. In a Kondo lattice with a $\mathbb Z_2$ spin liquid, the Kondo fields inherit the projective symmetry action of the spinons. When the projective time-reversal action on these fields squares to $-1$, the projective symmetry algebra forbids a condensate that preserves time-reversal symmetry and enforces twofold degeneracy of the critical modes. Because Kondo condensation in a $\mathbb Z_2$ spin liquid also breaks electromagnetic $U(1)$ symmetry, superconductivity and time-reversal symmetry breaking can emerge at a single continuous transition, even if crystal symmetry admits only one-dimensional irreducible representations. We demonstrate this mechanism in an anisotropic Kondo-Kitaev model, where superconductivity and the breaking of time-reversal and mirror symmetries emerge simultaneously.
summary: This theoretical work shows that in Kondo lattices coupled to $\mathbb{Z}_2$ spin liquids, symmetry fractionalization can force superconductivity and time-reversal symmetry breaking to occur together at one continuous transition. Using the Kondo-Kitaev model, the authors demonstrate this by analyzing the projective symmetry algebra and calculating multiple order parameters self-consistently.
main_problem: The paper addresses how superconductivity and the breaking of an additional symmetry, such as Time-Reversal Symmetry (TRS), can emerge simultaneously at a single continuous quantum phase transition.
main_result: Symmetry fractionalization provides a mechanism that forces the simultaneous onset of superconductivity and TRS breaking, even when conventional Landau theory predicts otherwise for low-symmetry systems.
method: The analysis employs theoretical derivations using projective symmetry algebra and mean-field theory applied to the Kondo lattice model.
model_or_system: The system is a Kondo lattice coupled to a $\mathbb{Z}_2$ spin liquid, modeled concretely using an anisotropic Kondo-Kitaev model on a honeycomb lattice.
key_observables: Superconducting order parameter ($P^{\mu}_{jk}$), Kondo amplitude ($\bar{h}$), and nonunitary triplet pairing vector ($\mathbf{q}_a$).
important_parameters: The condition $\Theta^2 = -I$ for the projective time-reversal action, and the critical temperature $T_c$.
main_assumptions: The analysis relies on the mean-field approximation and assumes the Kondo transition is approached from a deconfined $\mathbb{Z}_2$ spin liquid state.
figures_summary: Figure 1 shows mean-field results demonstrating that the Kondo amplitude, charge-two bond order, and nonunitary triplet pairing all become non-zero continuously at the same critical temperature $T_c$.
paper_structure: The paper develops the theory by first establishing the symmetry constraints via projective algebra, then applying mean-field theory to the Kondo-Kitaev model, and finally calculating the self-consistent order parameters to confirm the simultaneous transition.
why_interesting: The mechanism of symmetry fractionalization provides a powerful, non-standard theoretical tool for understanding emergent symmetries in strongly correlated materials, which is relevant to understanding exotic superconducting states.

figures.caption: FIG. 1. The panels show mean-field results for the Kondo–Kitaev model on 20 × 20 unit cells with periodic boundary conditions, Kx = Ky = 1, Kz = 0.95, tx = ty = 0.2, tz = 0.19, JK = 1.9, and conduction electron filling nc = 0.9 per site. (a) The mean-field scaling ¯h2 ∝Tc −T below Tc (inset) supports continuous onset of the Kondo amplitude ¯h. (b) Charge-two bond order Py a indicates Kondo-induced superconductivity. (c) Nonunitary triplet pairing qx a extracted from the anomalous c fermion correlators diagnoses broken TRS. Within numerical resolution, all three order parameters become nonzero continuously at the same critical temperature Tc ≃0.1358.
